qs.q: An environmental health study evaluates the combined carcinogenic effects of industrial exposures and lifestyle habits. When analyzing workers exposed to asbestos who also smoke cigarettes, how is the joint effect on lung cancer risk characterized?
o: Each exposure acts independently without altering overall risk.
Risks combine additively, increasing linearly with both factors.
Interaction is sub‑additive because of competing metabolic enzymes.
Tobacco exposure antagonizes asbestos, reducing the combined risk.
The two exposures interact multiplicatively, markedly raising cancer risk.
qs.e: Tobacco smoking and asbestos exposure act synergistically, resulting in a multiplicative rather than merely additive increase in lung cancer risk.

qs.q: An environmental health officer investigates a malaria outbreak and identifies larvae hanging parallel to the water surface without a siphon. Which genus is implicated?
qs.e: Anopheles larvae lack a breathing siphon and lie horizontally flat against the water surface to breathe.

qs.q: An environmental health officer investigates factors that help hookworm infective larvae survive and move on grass in warm, moist soil. Which mechanism enables this movement?
qs.e: Infective L3 larvae use capillary action in moist soil and vegetation to move around. They are vulnerable to direct sunlight, drying, and saltwater.
